A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HoP research, and their main text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains appendix pages, although v2 Section 4.4 refers to an appendix for data-efficiency details. Those promised details cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original HoP and Efficient HoP evaluations on LingoQA, DRAMA and BDD-X, together with component ablations and efficiency measurements in Sections 4.3–4.4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds training-data sensitivity results, attention visualizations, and evaluations of smaller and quantized language models.

M1.justification: The three hint sources, fusion procedures, and Efficient HoP distillation approach remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 4.1. Smaller and quantized language models are evaluated as configurations of the retained framework; no redesign of the HoP algorithm is described.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate autonomous-driving VQA on LingoQA, DRAMA and BDD-X and use Cityscapes for semantic-head training. Reduced training-data fractions change sample availability within existing coverage. Newly cited datasets such as nuScenes-QA are not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds fine-tuned LLaVA-v1.5 (+A-MoF) to the LingoQA comparison. Table 8 also adds VTS to the efficiency comparison, although VTS already appeared in the accuracy comparisons. The earlier comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds 25% and 50% LingoQA training-data conditions alongside full-data evaluation, and tests Efficient HoP with Qwen-v2.5-3B, Qwen-v2-0.5B and an AWQ-quantized 3B configuration. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and stated training settings remain unchanged. The missing appendix leaves subset-selection details unavailable.

E4.justification: v2 expands the analysis to substantive new questions about training-data requirements and language-model size/quantization tradeoffs through Figure 2 and the expanded Table 8. Figure 4 also adds CLIP-versus-HoP attention maps to the existing overtaking example. The original component, hint-source, token-count and fusion ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point performance scores and average inference latency without an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–7 are retained, with an added A-MoF row. New results include HoP scoring 64.0 with 25% training data versus full-data LLaVA's 63.2, and quantized 3B Efficient HoP scoring 64.2 at 281 ms. Table 8 revises LLaVA, HoP and Efficient HoP latencies from 1535/2251/1548 to 631/956/661 ms. These substantial reporting additions and revisions do not establish an explained same-setting speedup between versions.

T1.justification: The hint-token definitions and five fusion equations are mathematically unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no new derivation.

C1.justification: v2 makes data-efficient, rapid domain adaptation a central contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. It explicitly claims that HoP surpasses full-data LLaVA using only 25% of the training data. v1 emphasized improved driving representations, reasoning and benchmark performance without this sample-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 links general MLLM shortcomings more explicitly to scarce driving-domain data and missing domain priors, and interprets the reduced-data results as efficient domain adaptation. It also calls the quantized model's 281 ms latency deployment-ready. Existing explanations of hint complementarity and fusion behavior remain, without corresponding new deployment validation or limitations.

D1.justification: The expanded Table 8 identifies the exact Qwen variants and AWQ quantization used for the new configurations. Existing head architectures, optimizer settings and hardware disclosures are retained; the RTX 4090 statement added to Section 4.1 already appeared in v1's Table 8 caption. Detailed subsampling and quantization recipes are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including SPHINX, MoME, TOKEN, Pix2Struct, nuScenes-QA, AWQ and the A-MoF source, while removing SAM, BLIP-2 and SigLIP. The introduction and related work sharpen the distinction from feature-fusion approaches around driving-specific priors and adaptation with limited data.

P1.justification: v2 revises the motivation and contribution paragraphs, updates the abstract and conclusion, and rewrites parts of related work while retaining the section organization and most technical exposition. It also changes author ordering and affiliations, adds email addresses, and includes an acknowledgement.

P2.justification: v2 adds the training-data plot, augments the overtaking figure with attention maps, and expands Table 8 with language-model and performance columns. Existing figures are renumbered, moved or resized, and Table 7 rows are reordered. Best-score highlighting is corrected, including VTS's 20.5 METEOR in Table 1; this is not a numerical improvement.

improvement.justification: The added A-MoF comparison, reduced-data experiment, attention maps and model-size/quantization results make the evaluation more informative while preserving the original benchmark evidence. Corrected score highlighting also improves accuracy of presentation. These gains are limited by the absent referenced appendix, unexplained latency revisions and the deployment-readiness interpretation extending beyond the reported validation.
